requirements.quote:
An endpoint never sends packets that are protected with old keys.
   Only the current keys are used.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint protects a newly sent packet
requirements.required_behavior: Protect the packet using the endpoint's current packet-protection keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Protect and send the packet using old packet-protection keys.
requirements.why_checkable: Packets emitted after a key switch can be tested against current and old keys to verify that only the current key generation protects them.

requirements.quote:
Packets with higher packet numbers MUST be protected with either the
   same or newer packet protection keys than packets with lower packet
   numbers.
requirements.condition: For any two protected packets where one packet number is higher than the other
requirements.required_behavior: Protect the higher-numbered packet with the same key generation or a newer key generation than the lower-numbered packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Protect the higher-numbered packet with an older key generation than the lower-numbered packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet trace can order packets by packet number and compare the protection-key generation used for every ordered pair.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that successfully removes protection with old
   keys when newer keys were used for packets with lower packet numbers
   MUST treat this as a connection error of type KEY_UPDATE_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint successfully unprotects a packet with old keys after newer keys were used for a lower-numbered packet
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the detected key-generation regression as a connection error.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accept or continue processing the regressing packet as valid connection traffic.
requirements.error_behavior: Terminate the connection with error type KEY_UPDATE_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can send a lower-numbered packet with newer keys followed by a higher-numbered packet decryptable with old keys, and the resulting connection error code can be observed.
